--- ## Why Chrome Browser MCP? Most browser-use extensions force painful trade-offs: they either spin up logged-out headless browsers, permanently show Chrome's yellow debugger banner, burn 30K+ tokens per step with raw screenshots/HTML, conflict when two agents run simultaneously, or expose every private tab to prompt injection. | Capability | Chrome Browser MCP | Typical Browser Relay / Visual Extensions | | :------------------------------ | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Real Logged-In Sessions** | Works in your daily Chrome / Arc / Brave / Edge profile — no `--remote-debugging-port` hacks | Often needs separate debug profile or loses sessions | | **Hybrid Adaptive Engine** | Silent Content Script + WebMCP by default; **on-demand `chrome.debugger` CDP** with idle auto-detach & DevTools-open fallback | Always-on yellow debugger banner or brittle synthetic-only clicks | | **Token Efficiency** | Pruned a11y/DOM snapshot with short refs (`e1`, `e2`…), **incremental diffs**, and **batch `browser_act`** (multi-step forms in 1 round-trip) | Full DOM/screenshot every step; 1 LLM call per click | | **Multi-Agent & Multi-Profile** | Shared local Broker Daemon (Streamable HTTP + auto-spawn `stdio` shim with lease lifecycle) multiplexing multiple agents & browsers | Single-client port conflicts (`EADDRINUSE`) | | **Security & Control** | Dedicated colored **AI Agent Tab Group**, editable domain blocklist, risky-action approval gates, **Prompt-Injection Shield**, instant `Alt+Shift+P` Pause | Full unguarded browser access or constant friction | | **WebMCP & Workflow Recorder** | Native `navigator.modelContext` tool discovery + “Show by hand” workflow recorder with password masking | Manual clicking only | | **Antigravity MCP App UI** | Built-in **Browser Control Deck** (`ui://chrome-browser/deck.html`) in `aux_pane` & `global` views | Text-only tool output | --- ## Comparison with Other Browser Extensions There are several strong browser-automation extensions and MCP bridges in the ecosystem, each optimizing for a different workflow. Below is a technical comparison across the criteria that matter most for real-session AI browser use. | Criterion | **Chrome Browser MCP** | **Claude for Chrome** | **ChatGPT for Chrome** | **omp browser relay** | **Kimi Browser Ext.** | **Playwright MCP** (`--extension`) | **BrowserMCP** | | :------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------: | :-----------------------------------: | :---------------------------: | :--------------------------------------------: | :---------------------------------------: | :--------------------------------------------------: | :----------------------------------: | | **Open Source & License** | ✅ MIT | ❌ Closed | ❌ Closed | ✅ Open source | ❌ Closed _(community MCP wrappers)_ | ✅ Apache-2.0 | ✅ Open source | | **Agent-Agnostic MCP v2** | ✅ Any MCP host _(HTTP + `stdio` + Apps)_ | ⚠️ Claude / Claude Code only | ❌ ChatGPT only | ⚠️ `omp` CLI / raw CDP relay | ⚠️ Kimi ecosystem _(+ wrappers)_ | ✅ Any MCP host | ✅ Any MCP host | | **Real Logged-In Sessions** | ✅ Daily profile _(Chrome/Arc/Brave/Edge)_ | ✅ Daily profile | ✅ Daily profile | ✅ Daily profile _(bypasses Chrome 136+ lock)_ | ✅ Daily profile | ⚠️ Manual _"Share This Tab"_ _(isolated by default)_ | ✅ Daily profile | | **No Permanent Debugger Banner** | ✅ Hybrid CS + WebMCP; **on-demand CDP** auto-detach | ❌ Active CDP banner | ⚠️ Browser debugger perms | ❌ Always-on `chrome.debugger` | ❌ Always-on `chrome.debugger` | ❌ Always-on `chrome.debugger` | ❌ Always-on `chrome.debugger` | | **Works While DevTools Is Open** | ✅ Content Script fallback | ❌ CDP attach conflict | ⚠️ Limited | ❌ Single-debugger conflict | ❌ Single-debugger conflict | ❌ Single-debugger conflict | ❌ Single-debugger conflict | | **Token Efficiency (Diffs & Batching)** | ✅ Pruned refs + **incremental diffs** + **batch actions** | ⚠️ Full snapshots / screenshots | ⚠️ Backend-managed | ⚠️ Raw CDP _(depends on client)_ | ⚠️ Markdown/CSV extract; no diffs | ⚠️ Full a11y tree per step; 1 action/call | ⚠️ Full ARIA snapshot; 1 action/call | | **Multi-Agent & Multi-Profile** | ✅ Shared Broker Daemon _(leases + named profiles)_ | ❌ Single Claude session | ❌ Single ChatGPT session | ✅ Global daemon + Puppeteer mux | ❌ Single local bridge | ⚠️ Single shared tab in bridge mode | ❌ Single WS port / client | | **Tab Isolation & Human Controls** | ✅ **AI Agent** Tab Group, blocklist, approvals, `Alt+Shift+P` | ⚠️ Tab group + noisy per-site prompts | ⚠️ Prompts on sensitive pages | ❌ Basic relay attach | ⚠️ Basic sidebar/bridge controls | ⚠️ Manual per-tab share only | ⚠️ Manual popup connect | | **Prompt-Injection Shield** | ✅ Local untrusted-DOM sanitizer & hidden-text filter | ⚠️ Provider-side only | ⚠️ Provider-side only | ❌ None | ❌ None | ❌ None | ❌ None | | **Native WebMCP (`navigator.modelContext`)** | ✅ Built-in discovery & call | ❌ No | ❌ No | ❌ No | ❌ No | ❌ No | ❌ No | | **Workflow Recorder ("Show by hand")** | ✅ Side Panel recorder _(password masking + replay)_ | ⚠️ Saved prompts / shortcuts | ❌ No | ❌ No | ✅ Recorded Skills / CLI flows | ❌ Separate `codegen` tool | ❌ No | | **100% Local-First / No Cloud Account** | ✅ `127.0.0.1` + token, zero telemetry | ❌ Anthropic account | ❌ OpenAI account | ✅ 100% local | ⚠️ Local bridge; Kimi account for sidebar | ✅ 100% local | ✅ 100% local | ### How to Choose - **Choose Chrome Browser MCP** if you want an **open-source, model-agnostic MCP v2** extension for your real logged-in browser — with multi-agent concurrency, token-saving diffs & batching, silent default execution (no permanent debugger banner), built-in Prompt-Injection Shield, native WebMCP, and strict `127.0.0.1` privacy. - **Choose Claude for Chrome** or **ChatGPT for Chrome** if you work exclusively inside Anthropic's or OpenAI's first-party UI and want zero local CLI/daemon setup rather than cross-agent MCP interoperability. - **Choose omp browser relay** if you live inside the `oh-my-pi` (`omp`) ecosystem and specifically need a raw CDP/Puppeteer multiplexer over your real Chrome profile. - **Choose Kimi Browser Extension** if your workflow centers on Moonshot's Kimi sidebar, Kimi Work, and Kimi Skill/CLI routines. - **Choose Playwright MCP (isolated mode)** for deterministic headless/clean-profile E2E testing and CI pipelines where you intentionally do _not_ want personal cookies or active logins. - **Choose Chrome DevTools MCP (`chrome-devtools-mcp`)** _(non-extension CLI/CDP server)_ when your primary goal is deep frontend performance tracing, Lighthouse audits, and heap/network profiling rather than everyday authenticated browsing. > _Comparison snapshot as of late 2026. Browser-agent tools evolve quickly — if something above is outdated, PRs to keep this matrix accurate are welcome._ --- ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Clients["AI Agents / MCP Hosts"] AGY["Antigravity (MCP + Control Deck UI)"] CLI["Claude Code / Codex / Cursor"] end subgraph Broker["Local Broker Daemon (127.0.0.1:43179)"] MCP["Streamable HTTP /mcp + stdio shim"] HUB["Multi-Profile Router & Approval Engine"] WS["Authenticated WebSocket Hub (/ws)"] end subgraph Chrome["Chrome / Arc / Brave / Edge (MV3)"] SW["Service Worker (Keepalive + Tab Group)"] HUD["Side Panel Control HUD & Recorder"] CDP["On-Demand chrome.debugger (CDP)"] CS["Content Script (Snapshot, WebMCP, Shield, Visual HUD)"] end AGY --> MCP CLI --> MCP MCP --> HUB HUB --> WS WS <-->|"127.0.0.1 + Pairing Token"| SW SW <--> HUD SW --> CDP SW --> CS ``` --- ## Quick Start ### 1. Build from source ```bash git clone https://github.com/szybnev/chrome-browser-mcp.git cd chrome-browser-mcp pnpm install pnpm build ``` ### 2. Load the Chrome Extension (MV3) 1. Open `chrome://extensions` and enable **Developer mode**. 2. Click **Load unpacked** and select `packages/extension/dist`. 3. Click the **Chrome Browser MCP** icon in Chrome's toolbar to open the **Control HUD** Side Panel. ### 3. Pair with your local Broker (1-Click PIN or Token) Generate a 2-minute 6-digit pairing PIN (recommended for the post-install Welcome Wizard & Side Panel): ```bash node packages/server/dist/cli.js pair ``` Enter the 6-digit PIN in the **Welcome Tour** or **Pair** tab of the Chrome Side Panel (or expand **Advanced Connection** to paste a static token from `cli.js token`). ### 4. Connect your AI Agent #### Antigravity (Plugin + Browser Control Deck MCP App + Skill) Link `plugins/antigravity` into `~/.gemini/config/plugins/chrome-browser-mcp`: ```bash ln -s "$(pwd)/plugins/antigravity" ~/.gemini/config/plugins/chrome-browser-mcp ``` Antigravity automatically discovers: - The MCP server (`chrome-browser-mcp_browser`) - The **Browser Control Deck** MCP App in the side pane `+` menu (`aux_pane`) and left sidebar (`global`) - The `chrome-browser-mcp` agent skill playbook #### Claude Code / Cursor / Codex (`stdio` with automatic shared broker) Add to your MCP config (`mcp_config.json`, `.mcp.json`, or Claude Desktop config): ```json { "mcpServers": { "chrome-browser": { "command": "node", "args": ["/absolute/path/to/chrome-browser-mcp/packages/server/dist/cli.js", "stdio"] } } } ``` Multiple MCP clients share one local Broker Daemon automatically via lease heartbeats. #### Streamable HTTP MCP (2026 spec) Start the daemon directly: ```bash node packages/server/dist/cli.js daemon ``` Connect any Streamable HTTP MCP client to `http://127.0.0.1:43179/mcp`. --- ## MCP Tool Catalog | Tool | Purpose | | :-------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `browser_profiles` | List connected Chrome/Arc/Brave/Edge profiles and switch the active default profile | | `browser_tabs` | List, open, focus, close, attach, or detach tabs in the **AI Agent** tab group | | `browser_navigate` | Go to URL, back/forward, reload, or wait for selector/text | | `browser_snapshot` | Compact a11y/DOM snapshot across top frame, cross-origin `iframe`s (`f:e1`), and Shadow DOM, with incremental **diff** mode and **Prompt-Injection Shield** | | `browser_read` | Clean readable Markdown, structured HTML tables (`tables_csv` / `tables_json`), or PDF text extraction with pagination and hidden-DOM filtering | | `browser_screenshot` | Compressed WebP/JPEG/PNG screenshot with optional **Set-of-Mark** ref badges and `maxWidth` resizing | | `browser_act` | Execute 1 action or a **batch sequence** (`click`, `fill`, `type`, `press`, `select`, `check`, `scroll`, `hover`, `drag`, `upload`, `wait`) with **Zero-Secret `secretRef`**, optional in-page **Visual Agent Cursor**, and post-action diff snapshot | | `browser_dialog` | Inspect, accept, or dismiss native JS `alert` / `confirm` / `prompt` / `beforeunload` dialogs without hanging | | `browser_downloads` | List recent downloads or wait for completion (opt-in `downloads` permission) | | `browser_emulate` | Emulate mobile/desktop viewports (`iphone-15`, `pixel-9`, `ipad`, `reset`), `light`/`dark` scheme, network throttling (`slow-3g`/`offline`), or geolocation | | `browser_console` | Read captured browser console logs, warnings, and uncaught exceptions | | `browser_network` | Inspect XHR/fetch requests & failures, plus redacted response body inspection (`includeBodyForRequestId`) | | `browser_eval` | Evaluate JavaScript in page context via CDP (approval-gated on new origins & read-only domains) | | `browser_audit` / `browser_audit_export` | Quick a11y/CWV/storage audit and self-contained **JSON / HTML Session Replay** audit export | | `browser_webmcp_list` / `browser_webmcp_call` | Discover and invoke native client-side WebMCP tools (`navigator.modelContext`) | | `browser_workflows` | List, inspect, replay with `{{variables}}`, or export recorded flows to **Playwright `.spec.ts`** | | `browser_deck` | Open or refresh the **Browser Control Deck** interactive MCP App (EN / RU / 中文, Dark / Light) | --- ## Security, Supply-Chain & Git Hooks `pnpm install` automatically activates repository Git hooks via `core.hooksPath = .githooks`: - **`pre-commit`**: scans staged files for secrets/keys and unsafe patterns (`eval`, `innerHTML`, `0.0.0.0` binding, MV2 regressions), verifies lockfile integrity & CVEs if dependencies changed, then runs `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test`. - **`pre-push`**: runs full repository security scan, `sha512` lockfile & npm registry verification, unexpected `preinstall`/`install`/`postinstall` compromise check, `pnpm audit --audit-level=moderate`, plus full `typecheck`, `build`, and `test`. - **`pnpm-workspace.yaml`**: enforces `blockExoticSubdeps: true` and strict `allowBuilds` allowlisting (`esbuild` only). --- ## Monorepo Layout ```text chrome-browser-mcp/ ├── packages/ │ ├── protocol/ # Shared Zod v4 schemas, RPC envelope, Prompt-Injection Shield, diff engine │ ├── server/ # Local Broker Daemon (Streamable HTTP + stdio shim + WS Hub + CLI) │ ├── extension/ # Chrome MV3 Extension (Service Worker, On-Demand CDP, Content Script, HUD, Side Panel) │ └── mcp-app/ # Browser Control Deck (React + @modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps + vite-plugin-singlefile) ├── plugins/ │ └── antigravity/ # Ready-to-link Antigravity plugin (plugin.json, mcp_config.json, SKILL.md, logo) ├── scripts/ # Security/supply-chain checker, icon generator & Chrome Web Store ZIP packager ├── .githooks/ # Automatic pre-commit & pre-push security, audit, and test hooks ├── CHROMEWEBSTORE.md # Chrome Web Store listing, permission justifications & privacy disclosures └── PRIVACY.md # Local-first privacy policy (zero telemetry) ``` --- ## Development & Testing ```bash pnpm security:check # Secret scan + static guardrails + lockfile integrity + pnpm audit pnpm typecheck # Strict TypeScript check across all 4 packages pnpm build # Build protocol -> mcp-app -> server (bundles deck.html) -> extension pnpm test # Run Vitest unit + live Broker/MCP integration tests pnpm pack:cws # Package clean Chrome Web Store ZIP in release/ ``` --- ## Roadmap - Firefox & Safari WebExtension parity - Multi-step visual diff assertions for exported Playwright tests - Team-shareable signed security policy bundles ## License MIT — see [LICENSE](./LICENSE).

--- ## 为什么选择 Chrome Browser MCP？ 现有的 AI 浏览器自动化扩展往往存在明显痛点：要么启动未登录的无头浏览器，要么一直显示 Chrome 黄色调试横幅，要么每步发送巨量截图/原始 HTML 浪费数万 Token，要么多个 Agent 同时连接时发生端口冲突，或者将所有私密标签页暴露给网页提示词注入风险。 | 核心能力 | Chrome Browser MCP | 常见中继 / 视觉浏览器扩展 | | :--------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------ | | **真实登录会话** | 直接运行在日常使用的 Chrome / Arc / Brave / Edge 配置文件中，无需 `--remote-debugging-port` | 通常需要单独调试配置或丢失登录状态 | | **混合自适应引擎** | 默认使用无感 Content Script + WebMCP；仅在需要时**按需挂载 `chrome.debugger` (CDP)**，空闲自动断开，且兼容手动打开 DevTools | 始终显示黄色调试横幅，或合成点击不稳定 | | **极致 Token 效率** | 精简无障碍/DOM 快照与短引用（`e1`, `e2`…）、**增量 Diff**，以及**批量 `browser_act`**（单次调用填完表单并提交） | 每步拉取完整 DOM/截图，每次点击都消耗一次模型往返 | | **多 Agent 与多配置** | 共享本地 Broker 守护进程（Streamable HTTP + 自动拉起的租约式 `stdio` 垫片），支持多 Agent 与多浏览器并发复用 | 多客户端冲突（`EADDRINUSE`） | | **安全与人工可控** | 独立彩色 **AI Agent 标签组**、可编辑域名黑名单、敏感操作审批门控、**Prompt-Injection Shield**、`Alt+Shift+P` 一键紧急暂停 | 无隔离的全浏览器访问或过度弹窗干扰 | | **WebMCP 与工作流录制** | 原生发现并调用 `navigator.modelContext` 网页工具 + 侧边栏“手把手演示”工作流录制（自动掩码密码） | 只能逐元素手动点击 | | **Antigravity MCP App 面板** | 内置 **Browser Control Deck**（`ui://chrome-browser/deck.html`），支持 `aux_pane` 侧边栏与 `global` 全局视图 | 仅返回纯文本结果 | --- ## 与其他浏览器扩展的对比 目前 AI 浏览器自动化生态中已有不少优秀的扩展和 MCP 桥接工具，各自针对不同场景做了权衡。下表按真实会话 AI 浏览最关键的技术维度进行客观对比： | 评估维度 | **Chrome Browser MCP** | **Claude for Chrome** | **ChatGPT for Chrome** | **omp browser relay** | **Kimi Browser Ext.** | **Playwright MCP** --- ## Why Chrome Browser MCP? Most browser-use extensions force painful trade-offs: they either spin up logged-out headless browsers, permanently show Chrome's yellow debugger banner, burn 30K+ tokens per step with raw screenshots/HTML, conflict when two agents run simultaneously, or expose every private tab to prompt injection. | Capability | Chrome Browser MCP | Typical Browser Relay / Visual Extensions | | :------------------------------ | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Real Logged-In Sessions** | Works in your daily Chrome / Arc / Brave / Edge profile — no `--remote-debugging-port` hacks | Often needs separate debug profile or loses sessions | | **Hybrid Adaptive Engine** | Silent Content Script + WebMCP by default; 1 LLM call per click | | **Multi-Agent & Multi-Profile** | Shared local Broker Daemon (Streamable HTTP + auto-spawn `stdio` shim with lease lifecycle) multiplexing multiple agents & browsers | Single-client port conflicts (`EADDRINUSE`) | | **Security & Control** | Dedicated colored **AI Agent Tab Group**, editable domain blocklist, risky-action approval gates, **Prompt-Injection Shield**, instant `Alt+Shift+P` Pause | Full unguarded browser access or constant friction | | **WebMCP & Workflow Recorder** | Native `navigator.modelContext` tool discovery + “Show by hand” workflow recorder with password masking | Manual clicking only | | **Antigravity MCP App UI** | Built-in **Browser Control Deck** (`ui://chrome-browser/deck.html`) in `aux_pane` & `global` views | Text-only tool output | --- ## Comparison with Other Browser Extensions There are several strong browser-automation extensions and MCP bridges in the ecosystem, each optimizing for a different workflow. Below is a technical comparison across the criteria that matter most for real-session AI browser use. | Criterion | **Chrome Browser MCP** | **Claude for Chrome** | **ChatGPT for Chrome** | **omp browser relay** | **Kimi Browser Ext.** | **Playwright MCP** (`--extension`) | **BrowserMCP** | | :------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------: | :-----------------------------------: | :---------------------------: | :--------------------------------------------: | :---------------------------------------: | :--------------------------------------------------: | :----------------------------------: | | **Open Source & License** | ✅ MIT | ❌ Closed | ❌ Closed | ✅ Open source | ❌ Closed _(community MCP wrappers)_ | ✅ Apache-2.0 | ✅ Open source | | **Agent-Agnostic MCP v2** | ✅ Any MCP host _(HTTP + `stdio` + Apps)_ | ⚠️ Claude / Claude Code only | ❌ ChatGPT only | ⚠️ `omp` CLI / raw CDP relay | ⚠️ Kimi ecosystem _(+ wrappers)_ | ✅ Any MCP host | ✅ Any MCP host | | **Real Logged-In Sessions** | ✅ Daily profile _(Chrome/Arc/Brave/Edge)_ | ✅ Daily profile | ✅ Daily profile | ✅ Daily profile _(bypasses Chrome 136+ lock)_ | ✅ Daily profile | ⚠️ Manual _"Share This Tab"_ _(isolated by default)_ | ✅ Daily profile | | **No Permanent Debugger Banner** | ✅ Hybrid CS + WebMCP; Kimi account for sidebar | ✅ 100% local | ✅ 100% local | ### How to Choose - **Choose Chrome Browser MCP** if you want an **open-source, model-agnostic MCP v2** extension for your real logged-in browser — with multi-agent concurrency, token-saving diffs & batching, silent default execution (no permanent debugger banner), built-in Prompt-Injection Shield, native WebMCP, and strict `127.0.0.1` privacy. - **Choose Claude for Chrome** or **ChatGPT for Chrome** if you work exclusively inside Anthropic's or OpenAI's first-party UI and want zero local CLI/daemon setup rather than cross-agent MCP interoperability. - **Choose omp browser relay** if you live inside the `oh-my-pi` (`omp`) ecosystem and specifically need a raw CDP/Puppeteer multiplexer over your real Chrome profile. - **Choose Kimi Browser Extension** if your workflow centers on Moonshot's Kimi sidebar, Kimi Work, and Kimi Skill/CLI routines. - **Choose Playwright MCP (isolated mode)** for deterministic headless/clean-profile E2E testing and CI pipelines where you intentionally do _not_ want personal cookies or active logins. - **Choose Chrome DevTools MCP (`chrome-devtools-mcp`)** _(non-extension CLI/CDP server)_ when your primary goal is deep frontend performance tracing, Lighthouse audits, and heap/network profiling rather than everyday authenticated browsing. > _Comparison snapshot as of late 2026.
